h: History and Hills Round the Corner
p: High Wycombe sits among some of the best countryside in the Home Counties, and there's plenty of history close by too. Hughenden, a National Trust property on the edge of town, was the home of Victorian prime minister Benjamin Disraeli. It also has a fascinating wartime story, as it was used for secret map-making during the Second World War, and the grounds are lovely for a walk.

A little further west, West Wycombe has a picture-postcard village, the grand West Wycombe Park and the Hellfire Caves, a set of chalk tunnels with a colourful 18th-century back story. It's a quirky, slightly spooky outing that teenagers tend to enjoy.

On the track, the main thing to remember is to stay smooth. Kart steering is direct, so small movements are all you need. Brake before the corner, look through it, and feed the power in on the way out. Do that consistently and the lap times will tumble.
If you're bringing children, double-check the junior age and height requirements first, so no one is left disappointed on the day.

If you're travelling in from London, the M40 and the Chiltern Railways line make it an easy trip. Groups should book ahead at weekends, and allow a bit of extra time to park, sign in and get settled before the briefing starts.
